papers.title: Show-Harness: Just a VLM Agent Can Play Robots
papers.abstract: Abstract Show-Harness links vision-language models to robot control via discrete semantic actions interpreted by embodiment-specific modules, enabling zero-shot and efficient fine-tuned deployment across robots and GUIs.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Foundation vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit broad intelligence about the world, yet translating this intelligence into robot control remains challenging. We present Show-Harness, an Embodied Harness that enables VLMs to "play" robots through a compact semantic interface linking intent to action. Show-Harness exposes discrete semantic action units that VLMs can naturally reason over, while embodiment-specific interpreters deterministically ground them into local robot actions, keeping the VLM directly responsible for fine-grained physical decisions. Through the same interface, Show-Harness demonstrates the feasibility of (1) directly unlocking closed-source frontier VLMs for zero-shot robot control, and (2) adapting small-scale open-source VLMs for low-cost deployment with just a few GPU-hours of fine-tuning. We further develop GUMI (GUI Manipulation Interface), which extends the same semantic action space to GUI-based demonstration collection, allowing humans and agents to "play" robots across embodiments without specialized teleoperation hardware. Extensive experiments show that Show-Harness-equipped VLM agents generalize robustly across tasks, embodiments, and environments, outperforming representative agentic and VLA paradigms. These results suggest that the right interface can unlock substantial embodied capability from foundation VLMs, without requiring additional model capacity or costly embodiment-specific pretraining.
affiliations: Show Lab, National University of Singapore

ru.title: Семантический мост между языком и действием робота
ru.desc: Show-Harness представляет собой систему, которая соединяет видеоязыковые модели с управлением роботами через дискретные семантические действия, интерпретируемые специализированными модулями для каждого типа робота. Система позволяет использовать закрытые и открытые VLM для управления роботами как в режиме нулевого обучения, так и с эффективной дообучением на небольшом объёме данных. Авторы разработали GUMI — интерфейс для манипуляции GUI, который расширяет семантическое пространство действий на сбор демонстраций и позволяет управлять роботами без специализированного оборудования телеоперации. Экспериментальные результаты демонстрируют, что правильный семантический интерфейс позволяет раскрыть возможности фундаментальных моделей для воплощённых агентов без дополнительного обучения или специфичного для каждого робота преобучения.

en.title: Empowering Robots with Vision-Language Models through Show-Harness
en.desc: The paper introduces Show-Harness, a system that connects vision-language models (VLMs) to robot control using discrete semantic actions. This system allows VLMs to effectively translate their understanding of the world into actionable commands for robots, facilitating both zero-shot and fine-tuned deployments. Show-Harness includes embodiment-specific modules that interpret these actions, ensuring that VLMs can make precise physical decisions. Additionally, it extends to GUI manipulation, enabling seamless interaction with robots across different platforms without the need for specialized hardware.

zh.title: Show-Harness：解锁机器人控制的新方式
zh.desc: Show-Harness 是一种将视觉-语言模型与机器人控制连接起来的工具，通过特定的语义动作模块实现。这种方法使得视觉-语言模型能够在没有额外训练的情况下，直接控制机器人并进行高效的微调。Show-Harness 提供了一种紧凑的语义接口，将意图与动作相连接，使得模型能够自然地推理出离散的语义动作单元。通过这种接口，Show-Harness 证明了在不同任务和环境中，视觉-语言模型能够有效地进行机器人控制，展现出强大的通用性和适应性。

papers.title: Programmable World Model
papers.abstract: Abstract A programmable world model separates explicit state evolution from video generation using executable rules and 3D bounding boxes to maintain persistent, controllable environments.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Recent video world models generate increasingly realistic and interactive visual experiences, yet lack reliable mechanisms for maintaining persistent world state and enforcing programmable rules over extended interactions. We introduce Programmable World Model, a framework that decouples world-state evolution from visual observation generation. An agent translates natural-language instructions into executable programs that specify entity states and state-transition rules, enabling direct control over individual entities and their interactions. A lightweight engine executes these programs to update and maintain an explicit, persistent global world state, including off-screen entities and non-visual attributes. To connect world state with visual generation, we introduce state-augmented 3D oriented bounding boxes (OBBs) as an intermediate representation. This representation, together with the target camera trajectory, is deterministically compiled into pixel-aligned spatiotemporal conditioning signals for a pretrained video model serving as the generative renderer. This design allows users to create playable games with predefined mechanics, direct control over individual entities, and persistent world state throughout gameplay. We further introduce CombatStateBench, a benchmark for evaluating programmable world models. On CombatStateBench, our method achieves 94% Count Accuracy and 98% State Accuracy, substantially outperforming existing interactive video world models while supporting coherent long-horizon generation. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of separating explicit state evolution from generative rendering for building persistent, programmable worlds.

ru.title: Разделение логики мира и визуальной генерации для управляемых виртуальных окружений
ru.desc: В статье предлагается Programmable World Model — фреймворк, который разделяет эволюцию состояния мира от генерации видео. Агент преобразует естественный язык в исполняемые программы, которые управляют состоянием объектов и правилами их взаимодействия, сохраняя при этом стабильное глобальное состояние, включая сущности за пределами экрана. Для связи между состоянием и визуальной генерацией используются 3D ориентированные bounding boxes как промежуточное представление, которые детерминированно преобразуются в сигналы для предварительно обученной модели видео-генерации. Метод достигает 94% точности при подсчёте объектов и 98% точности состояния на новом бенчмарке CombatStateBench, обеспечивая генерацию на долгих горизонтах с полным контролем над каждой сущностью.

en.title: Building Interactive Worlds with Programmable State Control
en.desc: The paper presents a Programmable World Model that enhances video generation by separating the evolution of the world state from the visual output. It allows agents to interpret natural language commands into executable programs that manage the states and interactions of entities within a persistent environment. By using state-augmented 3D oriented bounding boxes, the model connects the world state to visual generation, enabling coherent and interactive gameplay. The proposed framework outperforms existing models in maintaining a consistent world state and supports long-term interactions, as demonstrated by the CombatStateBench benchmark results.

zh.title: 构建可编程的持久世界
zh.desc: 可编程世界模型通过可执行规则和3D边界框，将明确的状态演变与视频生成分离，从而维护持久且可控的环境。该框架允许代理将自然语言指令转化为可执行程序，指定实体状态和状态转移规则，实现对个体实体及其交互的直接控制。轻量级引擎执行这些程序，以更新和维护明确的全球世界状态，包括屏幕外实体和非视觉属性。通过引入状态增强的3D定向边界框，连接世界状态与视觉生成，从而实现用户创建具有预定义机制的可玩游戏。

papers.title: WearableQA: A Benchmark for Health Reasoning over Real-World Wearable Data
papers.abstract: Abstract WearableQA is a benchmark of multiple-choice questions derived from real longitudinal wearable data that evaluates large language model reasoning across data and health dimensions.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Recent advances in wearable sensing enable continuous monitoring of physiological and behavioral signals, yet existing benchmarks rarely evaluate whether AI systems can reason over a real user's longitudinal wearable record. We introduce WearableQA, a benchmark comprising 4,084 10-option multiple-choice questions constructed from the wearable time series, blood biomarkers, and demographics of 200 real users, each with up to 500 days of daily measurements. WearableQA preserves authentic wearable distributions that include device noise and inter-individual variability. To evaluate distinct reasoning capabilities, we introduce 16 question types organized along two complementary axes: data versus health reasoning, which distinguishes computation over longitudinal measurements from physiological interpretation; and single- versus cross-signal reasoning, which separates reasoning about individual signals from the integration of multiple signals. To construct reliable questions at scale, we adopt a dual-grounding framework that combines literature-grounded physiological findings with statistically validated population-grounded physiological patterns. This enables the capture of meaningful relationships observed in real-world wearable data. Evaluation of 14 proprietary and open-source LLMs demonstrates that WearableQA effectively differentiates model capabilities, with performance ranging from 19.6% to 72.9% against a 10% chance baseline. Moreover, WearableQA remains far from solved: most models achieve accuracies below 60%. Overall, WearableQA provides a realistic and diagnostic benchmark for evaluating LLM reasoning over real-world wearable data.

ru.title: Оценка рассуждения языковых моделей над реальными данными носимых датчиков
ru.desc: WearableQA — это бенчмарк для оценки способности больших языковых моделей рассуждать над реальными данными от носимых датчиков. Бенчмарк состоит из 4084 вопросов с множественным выбором, построенных на основе продольных данных 200 реальных пользователей, собранных за период до 500 дней. Вопросы организованы по двум осям: различие между вычислениями над данными и интерпретацией физиологических процессов, а также различие между анализом отдельных сигналов и интеграцией нескольких сигналов. Исследование показало, что LLM значительно отличаются по способности решать эту задачу, с точностью от 19,6% до 72,9%, что указывает на сложность и актуальность проблемы.

en.title: Evaluating AI Reasoning with Real Wearable Data
en.desc: WearableQA is a new benchmark designed to test how well large language models (LLMs) can reason using real data from wearable devices. It includes over 4,000 multiple-choice questions based on actual health and behavioral data from 200 users, collected over nearly 500 days. The benchmark assesses different reasoning skills, such as understanding individual health signals versus integrating multiple signals, and distinguishes between data analysis and health interpretation. Results show that while some models perform better than others, most still struggle, indicating that this area of AI reasoning is not yet fully developed.

zh.title: WearableQA：评估可穿戴数据推理能力的新基准
zh.desc: WearableQA是一个基准测试，旨在评估大型语言模型在真实可穿戴数据上的推理能力。它包含4084个多项选择题，基于200名用户的可穿戴时间序列、血液生物标志物和人口统计数据。该基准测试通过16种问题类型，考察数据与健康推理的不同能力，帮助理解个体信号与多信号整合的推理。评估结果显示，WearableQA有效区分了不同模型的能力，但大多数模型的准确率仍低于60%。

papers.title: SAEScientist-Bench: Can AI Agents Conduct Autonomous SAE Interpretability Research?
papers.abstract: Abstract The study introduces a benchmark to evaluate AI agents using sparse autoencoders for autonomous mechanistic interpretability and feature discovery, revealing progress but significant gaps versus expert baselines.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small While research on recursive self-improvement (RSI) has predominantly automated model training pipelines, reliable autonomous development demands a missing pillar: post-hoc monitoring and auditing to understand what models learn and ensure safe alignment. Mechanistic interpretability tools are essential to bridge this gap, among which Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) serve as a cornerstone by isolating interpretable features for model inspection and steering. In this paper, we introduce SAEScientist-Bench to evaluate whether AI agents can act as scientists utilizing SAE tools for autonomous mechanistic discovery. Given a target concept, an agent designs contrastive probes and navigates a Gemma Scope dictionary of 131K+ features in Gemma-2-9B-IT to discover the optimal feature, evaluated against curated expert reference features anchored on Neuronpedia across activation rank, concept selectivity on contrastive texts, and causal steering. Across 10 agent configurations and 20 tasks, frontier agents demonstrate genuine discovery capabilities and lead different evaluation dimensions, but remain well behind the expert baseline, approaching expert levels on separating target concepts from contrastive controls while lagging substantially in causal generation steering. Further analysis reveals that although agents can design contrasts to rule out spurious candidates, they frequently misinterpret experimental measurements. These results establish experimental model understanding as a measurable capability for closed-loop autonomous AI R&D. Our code is available at https://github.com/Trae1ounG/SAEScientist.
affiliations: School of Artificial Intelligence, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
The Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence, Institute of Automation, CAS

ru.title: Научный AI: автономное раскрытие механистики нейросетей через редкие автокодировщики
ru.desc: В статье представлен бенчмарк SAEScientist-Bench для оценки способности AI агентов действовать как учёные, используя Sparse Autoencoders (редкие автокодировщики) для автономного открытия механистических свойств нейронных сетей. Агенты должны разрабатывать контрастные пробы и искать оптимальные признаки в словаре из 131K+ характеристик модели Gemma-2-9B-IT, оцениваемые по рангу активации, селективности концепции и причинному управлению. Исследование показывает, что современные AI агенты демонстрируют настоящие способности к открытию, но значительно отстают от экспертных базовых линий, особенно в задачах причинного генерирования. Работа устанавливает экспериментальное понимание моделей как измеримую способность для замкнутого цикла автономных AI исследований и разработок.

en.title: Bridging the Gap: AI Agents in Mechanistic Discovery with Sparse Autoencoders
en.desc: This paper presents a new benchmark called SAEScientist-Bench to assess AI agents using Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) for mechanistic interpretability and feature discovery. The study highlights the importance of post-hoc monitoring to ensure that AI models learn safely and effectively. While the AI agents show some ability to discover features and design experiments, they still fall short compared to human experts in understanding and interpreting results. The findings suggest that while AI can assist in research and development, it requires further improvement to reach expert-level performance in causal generation and feature interpretation.

zh.title: 自主机制可解释性的AI代理评估基准
zh.desc: 本研究提出了一个基准，用于评估使用稀疏自编码器的人工智能代理在自主机制可解释性和特征发现方面的表现。尽管代理在某些任务上展示了真实的发现能力，但与专家基准相比仍存在显著差距。稀疏自编码器作为机制可解释性工具的基础，帮助代理识别可解释特征以进行模型检查和引导。研究结果表明，尽管代理能够设计对比实验以排除虚假候选者，但在实验测量的解读上常常出现误差。

papers.title: Scores Alone Do Not Prove Discovery: The Discovery Certification Protocol for Auditing AI Research Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract The Discovery Certification Protocol validates AI research agent outcomes through executable recovery tests, controlled audits, and deterministic verification with finite-sample recovery bounds.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small AI research agents combine prior knowledge, public sources, and experimental feedback to produce useful results. The Discovery Certification Protocol (DCP) turns claims about these results into executable recovery and feedback tests. Gate 1 validates useful improvement on sealed evaluation. Gate 2 gives matched agents the registered starting information and observed Web content while withholding the target research history. Every valid method reaching the numerical target supplies a recovery witness and triggers the Core veto. DCP Core requires adequate controls, zero observed recoveries, and a finite-sample bound on recovery in one fresh registered episode. Optional Gate 3 measures the average effect of truthful feedback relative to a specified neutral policy from a shared checkpoint. DCP Evidence adds this effect after independent null calibration and a registered effect margin. Two controlled audits exercise the complete protocol in SQLite optimization and virtual catalyst control under different models. Each produced zero recoveries in 96 episodes, with an upper bound of 0.0468. Each paired study yielded 30 truthful recoveries and zero neutral recoveries, with passing 60-pair null studies. Additional cases exercise Core, recovered, and audit-incomplete decisions. A deterministic, LLM-free verifier reproduces the decisions from frozen evidence. DCP provides a common evidence language for useful outcomes, alternative routes, and feedback effects across AI research.
affiliations: School of Computer Science, Carnegie Mellon University

ru.title: Сертификация открытий через верифицируемые тесты восстановления
ru.desc: В статье предложен Discovery Certification Protocol (DCP) — система валидации результатов AI research-агентов через выполняемые тесты восстановления, контролируемые аудиты и детерминированную верификацию. Протокол преобразует утверждения о результатах исследований в проверяемые тесты с конечной выборочной гарантией на восстановление результатов. Система использует многоступенчатый процесс: валидация улучшений на закрытом наборе данных, тестирование агентов с контролируемой информацией и измерение эффекта честной обратной связи. Экспериментальная проверка на задачах оптимизации SQL и контроля виртуальных катализаторов показала нулевые восстановления при верхней границе вероятности 0.0468.

en.title: Validating AI Outcomes with the Discovery Certification Protocol
en.desc: The Discovery Certification Protocol (DCP) is a framework designed to validate the outcomes of AI research agents through rigorous testing and verification methods. It employs executable recovery tests and controlled audits to ensure that the results produced by these agents are reliable and can be reproduced. The protocol includes multiple gates that assess the validity of improvements and the effectiveness of feedback mechanisms, ensuring that claims made by the agents are substantiated. By establishing a common evidence language, DCP facilitates the comparison of outcomes and enhances the credibility of AI research findings.

zh.title: 发现认证协议：确保AI研究结果的可靠性
zh.desc: 发现认证协议（DCP）通过可执行的恢复测试、受控审计和有限样本恢复界限的确定性验证来验证人工智能研究代理的结果。该协议将关于结果的声明转化为可执行的恢复和反馈测试，确保研究的有效性。DCP的核心要求有足够的控制、零观察恢复，并在一个新的注册事件中对恢复进行有限样本界限的约束。通过对不同模型下的SQLite优化和虚拟催化控制进行的两次受控审计，验证了协议的有效性，确保了结果的可靠性。

papers.title: DianShi-RxnDB: A Large-Scale, Fine-Grained Organic Reaction Data Platform Built via a Fully Automated Pipeline for Researchers and AI Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract DianShi-RxnDB is an automated platform that extracts and normalizes millions of structured organic reactions from patents to support AI-driven chemistry research.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small High-quality structured organic reaction data are essential for developing artificial intelligence for chemistry (AI4Chem), yet much of this knowledge remains dispersed across patent text, images, and reaction schemes. We present DianShi-RxnDB, a large-scale, fine-grained organic reaction data platform built via a fully automated extraction and normalization pipeline integrating patent text, images, and reaction schemes. Its corpus covers organic synthesis patents from the USPTO and EPO published between 1976 and 2025, yielding approximately 24 million reaction instances, of which approximately 14.8 million (61.7%) pass automated qualification checks. Each instance represents a specific single-step experiment recording participants, roles, quantities, temperatures, reaction times, yields, experimental procedures, and provenance links to source patents. In a manual evaluation of 1,300 sampled qualified instances, the micro-averaged field-level accuracy was 92.95%. A matched comparison with Pistachio further indicated advantages in deduplicated record counts, representation granularity, and field-level exact agreement. The platform provides a Web research workbench for searching, filtering, comparing, and source-verifying records, and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) service offering AI agents composable structured retrieval tools. DianShi-RxnDB is available at https://dianshi.opendatalab.org.cn/ .
affiliations: East China University of Science and Technology

ru.title: Структурированная химическая память: миллионы реакций для искусственного интеллекта
ru.desc: DianShi-RxnDB — это автоматизированная платформа для извлечения и нормализации миллионов структурированных органических реакций из патентов, которые служат ценным источником данных для обучения моделей AI4Chem. Система использует полностью автоматизированный конвейер обработки, объединяющий текст патентов, изображения и схемы реакций, извлекая информацию о реагентах, условиях синтеза, выходах и процедурах. Корпус содержит примерно 24 миллиона реакций из патентов USPTO и EPO (1976–2025 годы), из которых около 14,8 миллиона прошли автоматическую проверку качества с точностью 92,95%. Платформа предоставляет веб-интерфейс для поиска и анализа данных, а также MCP-сервис для интеграции с AI-агентами.

en.title: Unlocking Chemistry with Automated Reaction Data
en.desc: DianShi-RxnDB is an innovative platform designed to automate the extraction and normalization of organic reaction data from patents, facilitating AI research in chemistry. It compiles a vast dataset of approximately 24 million reaction instances, with a significant portion passing quality checks, ensuring high reliability for AI applications. The platform integrates various data sources, including text and images from patents, to provide detailed information on chemical reactions, such as reactants, conditions, and yields. Additionally, it offers a user-friendly web interface for researchers to access, filter, and analyze this structured data effectively.

zh.title: DianShi-RxnDB：化学研究的智能数据平台
zh.desc: DianShi-RxnDB是一个自动化平台，旨在从专利中提取和规范化数百万个结构化有机反应，以支持基于人工智能的化学研究。该平台通过完全自动化的提取和规范化流程，整合了专利文本、图像和反应方案，构建了一个大规模的有机反应数据平台。它涵盖了1976年至2025年间发布的美国专利商标局和欧洲专利局的有机合成专利，提供约2400万个反应实例，其中约1480万个（61.7%）通过了自动化资格检查。DianShi-RxnDB还提供了一个Web研究工作台，方便用户搜索、过滤、比较和验证记录。

papers.title: Revisiting Complete Reasoning Traces for Post-Training
papers.abstract: Abstract Large language models gain reasoning improvements from truncated trajectory endpoints rather than full reasoning traces, reducing redundancy while benefiting supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Large language models (LLMs) are often post-trained on pre-collected reasoning trajectories to improve their reasoning capability. Such trajectories tend to be long due to complex, interwoven paths, which often include detours on the path toward the answer. However, it has been underexplored whether LLMs indeed benefit from learning complete trajectories in post-training, such as supervised fine-tuning (SFT). Starting from our pilot study, we find that full trajectories provide only limited benefit, while partial trajectories are effective even under heavy truncation. We analyze redundancy in reasoning trajectories through attention-based analyses and controlled token-removal studies, both of which show that intermediate tokens contribute minimally to final reasoning quality. This suggests that avoiding redundant information may allow LLMs to internally infer coherent alternatives by inferring missing steps from their internal knowledge, given known trajectory endpoints. Furthermore, we show that training LLMs using endpoints leads to consistent changes in reasoning behavior, and that it also benefits post-training methods based on reinforcement learning or on-policy distillation, highlighting the need to revisit complete reasoning traces. Code is available at https://github.com/naver-ai/revisiting-trace.

ru.title: Краткие концовки лучше полных путей: как избежать избыточности при обучении рассуждениям
ru.desc: В этой работе исследуется, как большие языковые модели учатся на траекториях рассуждений при постобучении. Авторы показали, что полные траектории менее эффективны, чем усечённые траектории, заканчивающиеся ответом, так как промежуточные токены содержат много избыточной информации. Анализ внимания и контролируемое удаление токенов подтвердили, что LLM могут восстанавливать пропущенные шаги из своих внутренних знаний. Такой подход улучшает как supervised fine-tuning, так и методы обучения с подкреплением, предполагая необходимость пересмотра стандартного использования полных траекторий.

en.title: Optimize Reasoning: Focus on Endpoints, Not Full Paths!
en.desc: This paper explores how large language models (LLMs) can improve their reasoning abilities by focusing on truncated trajectory endpoints instead of complete reasoning paths. The authors find that using partial trajectories, even when heavily truncated, is more effective than relying on full reasoning traces, which often contain redundant information. Through various analyses, they demonstrate that intermediate reasoning steps contribute little to the final outcome, suggesting that LLMs can infer missing information from their existing knowledge. The study highlights the importance of optimizing training methods, particularly in supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, by emphasizing endpoint training over complete trajectories.

zh.title: 优化推理：截断轨迹端点的优势
zh.desc: 这篇论文探讨了大型语言模型（LLMs）在推理能力提升方面的研究。研究发现，与完整的推理轨迹相比，截断的轨迹端点能够减少冗余信息，同时在监督微调和强化学习中仍然有效。通过分析推理轨迹中的冗余性，研究表明中间的推理步骤对最终结果的贡献有限。最终，使用轨迹端点进行训练可以显著改变推理行为，并对后续的训练方法产生积极影响。

papers.title: SyncWorld: Visual Calibration Enables World Models as Zero-Shot Simulators
papers.abstract: Abstract SyncWorld is an action-conditioned world model that uses visual calibration episodes to learn environment-specific action-to-visual mappings, enabling zero-shot simulation and test-time policy improvement across unseen robotic settings.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small World models are increasingly used as policy-in-the-loop imagination environments, where reliable rollouts require fine-grained controllability with respect to low-level robot actions. A key obstacle to scaling such models in robotics is that actions are not a universal language in pixel space: changes in visual environment, camera view, robot placement, or embodiment alter how the same numerical action manifests visually, leading to conflicting supervision under mixed training and brittle generalization at deployment. We introduce SyncWorld, an action-conditioned world model that serves as a zero-shot simulator across unseen environments without any additional training. SyncWorld leverages a visual calibration episode---paired frames and actions that showcase all the controllable degrees of freedom---to specify the setup-specific Action--Visual Mapping in context. Training with visual calibration contexts teaches the model to interpret actions through visual evidence and to leverage interaction history when explicit calibration is unavailable. Experiments show that SyncWorld can accurately simulate action outcomes in previously unseen settings, and that its capability of simulating rollouts enables test-time policy improvement without training.

ru.title: Универсальная модель мира для робототехники через визуальную калибровку
ru.desc: SyncWorld — это модель мира, обусловленная действиями робота, которая использует визуальные калибровочные эпизоды для обучения отображению действий в визуальный домен, специфичному для каждой среды. Ключевая проблема масштабирования таких моделей в робототехнике заключается в том, что одни и те же численные действия производят разные визуальные эффекты в зависимости от конфигурации среды, положения камеры и типа робота. Модель обучается на основе визуальных контекстов калибровки, которые демонстрируют все управляемые степени свободы, позволяя интерпретировать действия через визуальные доказательства. Экспериментальные результаты показывают, что SyncWorld может точно симулировать результаты действий в ранее невиданных условиях и улучшать политику управления во время тестирования без переобучения.

en.title: Zero-Shot Simulation for Robotic Adaptability
en.desc: SyncWorld is a novel action-conditioned world model designed to enhance robotic simulations by learning specific action-to-visual mappings for different environments. It utilizes visual calibration episodes to understand how actions translate into visual changes, allowing it to operate effectively in new settings without needing additional training. This model addresses the challenge of inconsistent action representations caused by variations in the environment, camera angles, or robot configurations. By enabling zero-shot simulation and improving policies at test time, SyncWorld demonstrates significant advancements in the reliability and adaptability of robotic systems.

zh.title: SyncWorld：无缝适应新环境的智能模拟器
zh.desc: SyncWorld是一种基于动作的世界模型，通过视觉校准集来学习特定环境的动作与视觉之间的映射，从而实现零-shot模拟和测试时策略改进。该模型解决了机器人领域中动作在像素空间中不是通用语言的问题，使得在不同视觉环境下的动作表现一致。SyncWorld利用视觉校准集来指定特定设置的动作-视觉映射，帮助模型通过视觉证据理解动作。实验表明，SyncWorld能够在未见过的环境中准确模拟动作结果，并在测试时实现策略改进，而无需额外训练。

papers.title: Φ-Bench: Can Large Language Models Engineer the Infrastructure That Powers Them?
papers.abstract: Abstract Φ-Bench evaluates large language models on open-ended engineering of the LLM infrastructure stack across tasks from kernel optimization to end-to-end system design.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in reasoning and code generation, raising the prospect that they could assist in developing and optimizing the very infrastructure that powers them. However, existing benchmarks mainly focus on isolated kernels, predefined operators, or pre-specified optimization targets, and therefore fail to evaluate the ability of LLMs to perform open-ended, long-horizon LLM infrastructure engineering. To address this gap, we present Φ-Bench, a benchmark for systematically evaluating LLMs on engineering the LLM infrastructure stack. Derived from optimization problems studied in frontier research and grounded in real-world code repositories, Φ-Bench provides broad coverage of the LLM infrastructure stack and spans tasks of varying complexity, ranging from localized kernel-level function completion to long-horizon implementation and end-to-end system optimization. Extensive experiments on frontier LLMs reveal their current capabilities and limitations in engineering complex LLM infrastructure, offering insights into the challenges that remain on the path toward autonomous optimization of future AI infrastructure.
affiliations: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
University of Science and Technology of China

ru.title: Языковые модели как инженеры собственной инфраструктуры
ru.desc: Φ-Bench — это бенчмарк для оценки способностей больших языковых моделей в инженерии инфраструктуры LLM, от оптимизации ядер до проектирования полноценных систем. В отличие от существующих наборов задач, которые сосредоточены на изолированных компонентах, Φ-Bench оценивает открытые, долгосрочные задачи оптимизации реальной инфраструктуры LLM. Бенчмарк основан на фронтальных исследованиях и включает задачи различной сложности, от заполнения функций на уровне ядра до реализации и оптимизации всей системы. Эксперименты показывают текущие возможности и ограничения современных LLM в автономной оптимизации инфраструктуры искусственного интеллекта.

en.title: Empowering LLMs to Engineer Their Own Infrastructure
en.desc: Φ-Bench is a new benchmark designed to evaluate large language models (LLMs) on their ability to engineer and optimize their own infrastructure. Unlike previous benchmarks that focus on specific tasks or predefined goals, Φ-Bench assesses LLMs on a wide range of open-ended engineering challenges, from kernel optimization to complete system design. This benchmark is based on real-world code and complex optimization problems, providing a comprehensive evaluation of LLM capabilities. The results from testing various LLMs highlight their strengths and weaknesses in handling intricate infrastructure tasks, shedding light on the future of autonomous AI optimization.

zh.title: 评估大型语言模型的基础设施工程能力
zh.desc: Φ-Bench是一个用于评估大型语言模型（LLM）在开放式工程任务中的能力的基准测试。它涵盖了从内核优化到端到端系统设计的多种任务，旨在填补现有基准测试的空白。通过对前沿研究中的优化问题进行分析，Φ-Bench能够系统地评估LLM在工程基础设施堆栈中的表现。实验结果揭示了当前LLM在复杂基础设施工程中的能力和局限性，为未来AI基础设施的自主优化提供了重要见解。

papers.title: Co-Evolving Harnesses and Models: On-Policy Correction Helps Weaker Models Catch Up Where Imitation Fails
papers.abstract: Abstract Combining harness evolution with localized expert correction improves weaker models without disrupting their native planning style.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Agent harnesses (the system prompt, tool set, execution hooks, and context-management scaffolding around a model) are a critical determinant of agentic task success. Automated harness evolution can enable smaller models to perform well on domain-specific tasks at a fraction of frontier-model cost. Since both the harness and model weights shape behavior, we ask how harness evolution and lightweight fine-tuning should be combined. Across seven enterprise agent tasks, we first evolve a harness with the weaker model, then find that a stronger expert often uses it more effectively, suggesting expert supervision could close the remaining gap. However, training the weaker model on the expert's complete trajectories under the evolved harness backfires: performance regresses on all seven tasks by 4 to 30 points across Qwen3-Coder and Gemma 4, even though the same procedure helps under the unevolved harness. Our analysis shows that imitation transfers knowledge and increases scaffold usage, but disrupts model-harness fit: the weaker model adopts the expert's planning strategy without the competence to execute it and no longer matches the harness evolved around its native planning style. We therefore develop an on-policy expert-correction pipeline, automated by a meta-level MLE agent, that localizes the failing turn in the weaker model's own rollout and asks the expert to rewrite only that turn. This preserves the model's planning style and combines the gains of harness evolution and model adaptation. Our results identify and resolve a source of contention between harness and weight updates, yielding a compatibility-preserving recipe for economical co-evolution on domain-specific enterprise tasks.

ru.title: Согласованная эволюция: как развивать слабые модели без нарушения их планирования
ru.desc: В работе исследуется, как эволюция системного промпта (harness) и локальная адаптация моделей могут совместно улучшить производительность слабых моделей на специализированных задачах. Авторы показывают, что при наивном обучении на полных траекториях эксперта производительность падает, потому что слабая модель теряет соответствие со своим эволюционировавшим harness'ем. Они предлагают альтернативный подход: на-полис конвейер коррекции эксперта, который выявляет ошибки в собственных прогонах модели и просит эксперта переписать только эти шаги. Такой метод сохраняет исходный стиль планирования модели и успешно комбинирует выгоды эволюции harness и адаптации весов.

en.title: Enhancing Weaker Models with Expert-Corrected Harness Evolution
en.desc: This paper discusses a method to enhance weaker machine learning models by combining harness evolution with expert corrections. The harness, which includes the system's tools and context management, plays a crucial role in the model's success on specific tasks. The authors found that while evolving the harness improves performance, directly training the weaker model on expert trajectories can lead to worse results due to a mismatch in planning styles. To address this, they propose a new approach that allows the model to maintain its native planning style while still benefiting from expert guidance, leading to better performance on enterprise tasks.

zh.title: 结合工具演化与专家修正，提升模型表现
zh.desc: 本文探讨了如何通过结合工具演化与局部专家修正来提升较弱模型的表现，而不干扰其原有的规划风格。研究表明，生成的工具（即系统提示、工具集、执行钩子和上下文管理框架）是影响智能体任务成功的重要因素。通过自动化工具演化，较小的模型能够以较低的成本在特定领域任务中表现良好。我们提出了一种基于专家修正的管道，能够在保持模型规划风格的同时，结合工具演化和模型适应的优势。

papers.title: AgenticGen: Reward-Guided Agentic Video Generation for Advertising
papers.abstract: Abstract AgenticGen improves advertising video generation by decomposing it into strategy selection and draft generation stages supervised by online business feedback and human quality rewards.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Advertising video generation is not only a video synthesis task, but also a product-conditioned reasoning problem whose success is measured by online business metrics. Recent video foundation models can generate realistic clips from multimodal conditions, yet they do not optimize how a product should be transformed into an effective advertisement or how future generation should be improved from online business feedback. To close this loop, we propose AgenticGen, a reward-guided agentic framework that decomposes advertising video generation into two trainable reasoning stages, strategy selection and draft generation, thereby exposing optimization targets that online business feedback can supervise. AgenticGen learns a performance-based reward from accumulated online feedback and a complementary rubric-based reward aligned with human quality standards, then uses them to supervise policy optimization. DPO first moves the agentic policies toward online preferences, and GRPO further refines both stages with process and outcome rewards. Offline experiments validate the reward models and successive policy optimization. Online A/B experiments in the TikTok advertising system show that AgenticGen after DPO and GRPO improves CTR by 2.72%, CVR by 2.63%, and Advv by 9.61% over the SFT baseline.
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong

ru.title: Агентная генерация видеорекламы с обратной связью от реального бизнеса
ru.desc: AgenticGen — это система для генерации рекламных видео, которая разбивает задачу на два этапа: выбор стратегии и создание черновика. Модель использует два типа награждающих функций — одну на основе реальных бизнес-метрик из онлайна и другую на основе критериев качества от экспертов. Для оптимизации политики применяются методы DPO и GRPO, которые учитывают как процесс генерации, так и финальный результат. В экспериментах на платформе TikTok система показала улучшение ключевых метрик на 2-10% по сравнению с базовым подходом.

en.title: Optimizing Advertising Videos with AgenticGen
en.desc: AgenticGen is a novel framework designed to enhance the generation of advertising videos by breaking the process into two key stages: strategy selection and draft generation. This approach is guided by real-time business feedback and human quality assessments, ensuring that the generated content is not only visually appealing but also effective in promoting products. By utilizing a reward-based system that incorporates both online performance metrics and human evaluations, AgenticGen optimizes the video generation process to better align with audience preferences. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in click-through rates (CTR), conversion rates (CVR), and advertising value (Advv) compared to traditional methods.

zh.title: 智能广告视频生成的新方法
zh.desc: AgenticGen 是一种改进广告视频生成的方法，它将生成过程分为策略选择和草稿生成两个阶段，并通过在线商业反馈和人类质量奖励进行监督。该方法不仅关注视频合成，还考虑如何将产品转化为有效的广告，并根据在线业务指标来评估成功。AgenticGen 通过积累的在线反馈学习性能奖励，并结合人类质量标准的评估奖励，来优化生成策略。实验结果表明，AgenticGen 在 TikTok 广告系统中显著提高了点击率和转化率。

papers.title: Diffs vs. Whole Files: An Empirical Comparison of Iterative Edit-Based and Direct Generation for Flutter/Dart Code Models
papers.abstract: Abstract Diff-based code editing underperforms direct generation overall but excels only on short, localized edits such as refactoring and error fixes, a property termed task locality.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Large language models used for code editing can be trained and deployed in at least two output regimes: direct generation, where the model emits the entire modified file in one shot, and iterative diff-based generation ("steps"), where the model emits a sequence of localized search/replace edits applied one at a time until it signals completion or a step budget is exhausted. The diff-based regime is attractive because it mirrors how developers edit code and should require far fewer generated tokens per turn. We train two code models - a 100M-parameter model trained from scratch (Rainbow-Pony-100M) and a fine-tuned Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B - in both regimes on a shared Flutter/Dart dataset, and evaluate all four resulting models on a held-out set of approx 1,790 tasks per model. Direct generation substantially outperforms diff-based generation on every metric we measure - compilation/static-analysis pass rate, bits-per-byte, character-level similarity to the reference, and blinded LLM-judge ratings of goal fulfillment, correctness, and code quality - and the gap persists after controlling for task difficulty via a matched-ID comparison and when restricting to code that compiles on both sides. We then identify a single, architecture-independent mechanism behind the conditions where diff-based generation does win: it is competitive on short, spatially localized edits, and its category-level wins concentrate in exactly the two task categories - refactoring and error-handling/edge-case fixes - with the lowest mean edit-step count in our dataset. We term this task locality and discuss its implications for when an edit-based training regime is and is not the right choice for a code-editing model.

ru.title: Локальность задачи определяет выбор между прямой генерацией и diff-based редактированием кода
ru.desc: В исследовании сравнивается прямая генерация и diff-based подход при обучении больших языковых моделей для редактирования кода. Авторы обучили несколько моделей на наборе данных Flutter/Dart и обнаружили, что прямая генерация значительно превосходит diff-based метод по всем метрикам, включая успешность компиляции и качество кода. Однако diff-based подход показывает конкурентные результаты при работе с короткими, локализованными правками, такими как рефакторинг и исправление ошибок. Авторы вводят концепцию «task locality» для объяснения того, когда каждый подход наиболее эффективен при редактировании кода.

en.title: Task Locality: When Diff-Based Code Editing Shines
en.desc: This paper investigates the performance of two code editing approaches using large language models: direct generation and diff-based generation. While direct generation produces better results overall, diff-based generation shows strengths in making short, localized edits, particularly in refactoring and error fixes, a phenomenon referred to as task locality. The authors trained two models on a Flutter/Dart dataset and evaluated their performance across various metrics, finding that direct generation consistently outperformed diff-based methods. The study highlights the specific scenarios where diff-based generation can be effective, emphasizing its utility for certain types of code modifications.

zh.title: 任务局部性：代码编辑的关键
zh.desc: 这篇论文探讨了基于差异的代码编辑与直接生成的性能比较。研究发现，尽管直接生成在大多数情况下表现更好，但在短小的局部编辑任务（如重构和错误修复）中，基于差异的生成方法表现优异。作者提出了“任务局部性”的概念，指出基于差异的生成在特定任务类别中更具竞争力。最后，论文讨论了何时选择基于编辑的训练方法对代码编辑模型是合适的。

papers.title: Puppeteer: Object-Grounded Posture-Aware Co-Speech Gesture Generation
papers.abstract: Abstract Puppeteer is a diffusion-based co-speech gesture model that uses causal latent tokens and object geometry to generate temporally coherent, physically grounded gestures.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Generating co-speech gestures that are temporally coherent, semantically aligned with speech, and grounded with surrounding objects remains challenging. Prior speech-driven gesture models emphasize audio-gesture alignment but do not explicitly account for posture constraints or surrounding objects, failing to capture the inherent correlation between body gestures and the physical space. We present Puppeteer, a posture-aware, object-grounded co-speech gesture diffusion model operating in a causal latent space. We decompose long gestures into structured primitives and learn a causal variational autoencoder that encodes them into temporally ordered latent tokens, each depending only on the past. We then perform conditional diffusion directly in the causal latent space, conditioning on speech signals, motion history, an initial posture reference, and object geometry to synthesize physically consistent gestures. This temporally ordered latent formulation enables explicit temporal control and supports tasks such as gesture in-betweening and gesture completion. To better assess co-speech gesture synthesis beyond existing measures, we introduce new evaluation metrics tailored to this task. We also created SceneGes, the first curated synthetic 3D dataset of embodied co-speech gestures and corresponding 3D objects, enabling object-grounded gesture generation. Experiments show that Puppeteer generates more diverse and temporally synchronized gestures than prior methods, while enabling object-grounded gesture synthesis.

ru.title: Жесты в речи, управляемые окружающей средой
ru.desc: Puppeteer — это модель диффузии для синтеза жестов в речи, которая использует причинные латентные токены и геометрию объектов для создания временно согласованных и физически обоснованных жестов. Модель разлагает длинные жесты на структурированные примитивы и обучает причинный вариационный автокодировщик, кодирующий их в упорядоченные во времени латентные токены. Синтез выполняется методом условной диффузии в причинном латентном пространстве, обусловленной речевыми сигналами, историей движений, начальной позой и геометрией окружающих объектов. Авторы представили новые метрики оценки и создали первый кураторский синтетический 3D датасет SceneGes с жестами и соответствующими объектами для обучения.

en.title: Puppeteer: Grounded Gestures for Speech with Causal Latent Modeling
en.desc: Puppeteer is a novel model designed to generate co-speech gestures that are both temporally coherent and physically grounded in their environment. It utilizes a causal latent space to encode gestures into structured primitives, allowing for better alignment with speech and surrounding objects. By incorporating posture constraints and object geometry, Puppeteer enhances the realism and diversity of generated gestures. Additionally, it introduces new evaluation metrics and a synthetic dataset, SceneGes, to improve the assessment of gesture synthesis performance.

zh.title: Puppeteer：生成物体基础的共语手势
zh.desc: Puppeteer是一种基于扩散的共语手势模型，利用因果潜在标记和物体几何生成时间一致、物理基础的手势。该模型解决了生成与语音语义一致且与周围物体相关的手势的挑战。Puppeteer通过将长手势分解为结构化原语，并学习因果变分自编码器，将其编码为时间有序的潜在标记，从而实现手势的生成。实验表明，Puppeteer生成的手势比以往方法更具多样性和时间同步性，同时支持基于物体的手势合成。

papers.title: RESCUE-BENCH: Towards Relation-Aware Multi-Party Emotional Support Conversation Systems
papers.abstract: Abstract This work introduces a benchmark for evaluating whether large language models can understand evolving interpersonal dynamics to provide effective emotional support in multi-party settings.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Existing emotional support conversation systems mainly focus on one-on-one seeker-supporter interactions and individual emotional states, leaving interpersonal relations in multi-party scenarios underexplored. In this work, we introduce relation-aware emotional support conversation, a new task that evaluates whether LLMs can capture and utilize the evolving dynamics of relationships to offer more effective emotional support. We construct RESCUE (Relation-aware Emotional Support Conversation Understanding and Evaluation Benchmark) from real couple and family interview conversations, containing 191 samples, 7,079 annotated turns, and 1,064.8 minutes of video. Based on rich annotations of socio-emotional and support-related dynamics, RESCUE defines six tasks that evaluate two core capabilities required for relation-aware emotional support: Relational Understanding and Relation-Sensitive Support. Experiments with ten LLMs show that current models perform relatively well on tasks relying on local emotional or intervention cues, but struggle with relation-intensive tasks such as relation pattern prediction, viewpoint prediction, and support strategy prediction. These findings reveal the limitations of current LLMs in modeling interpersonal relations and making relation-sensitive support decisions.

Department of Computing, Hong Kong Polytechnic University
Research Institute for Quantum Technology, Hong Kong Polytechnic University
School of Computer Science and Engineering, Nanjing University of Science and Technology
School of Design, Hong Kong Polytechnic University
XU Exponential University of Applied Sciences

ru.title: Понимание межличностных отношений для эмоциональной поддержки в групповых диалогах
ru.desc: В работе представлен бенчмарк RESCUE для оценки способности больших языковых моделей понимать динамику межличностных отношений и оказывать эффективную эмоциональную поддержку в многосторонних сценариях. Существующие системы эмоциональной поддержки сосредоточены на диадических взаимодействиях между помогающим и нуждающимся, тогда как задача понимания отношений в семейных и групповых ситуациях остаётся малоизученной. Авторы сконструировали датасет из реальных записей интервью пар и семей с 7079 аннотированными репликами и определили шесть задач для оценки двух ключевых компетенций: понимания отношений и чувствительности к динамике взаимодействия. Эксперименты показали, что современные LLM хорошо справляются с локальным анализом эмоций, но испытывают сложности с предсказанием паттернов отношений, точек зрения собеседников и выбором адекватных стратегий поддержки.

en.title: Enhancing Emotional Support through Relational Understanding
en.desc: This paper presents a new benchmark called RESCUE, designed to assess how well large language models (LLMs) can understand and respond to emotional needs in multi-party conversations. Unlike traditional systems that focus on one-on-one interactions, RESCUE emphasizes the importance of interpersonal dynamics in providing effective emotional support. The benchmark includes real conversations with detailed annotations, allowing for the evaluation of two key capabilities: Relational Understanding and Relation-Sensitive Support. Experiments show that while LLMs perform adequately on simple emotional cues, they struggle with more complex relational tasks, highlighting their limitations in understanding interpersonal relationships.

zh.title: 关系感知情感支持对话的探索
zh.desc: 本研究提出了一个基准，用于评估大型语言模型是否能够理解不断变化的人际关系动态，以在多方环境中提供有效的情感支持。现有的情感支持对话系统主要集中在一对一的求助者与支持者之间，忽视了多方场景中的人际关系。我们引入了关系感知情感支持对话这一新任务，评估大型语言模型是否能够捕捉和利用关系的动态变化来提供更有效的情感支持。通过构建RESCUE基准，我们定义了六个任务，评估关系理解和关系敏感支持这两项核心能力。

papers.title: Difficulty-Adaptive Tree-Structured Policy Optimization for Expanding Reasoning Coverage in RLVR
papers.abstract: Abstract DATPO improves reasoning coverage in large models by using difficulty-adaptive tree-structured rollouts with sentence-entropy-guided branching and diversity-aware optimization.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has been central to the recent success of Large Reasoning Models. However, while RLVR significantly improves single-sample accuracy, it often fails to expand the model's intrinsic reasoning coverage (pass@k) due to limited exploration during training. To address this, we optimize the structural design of train-time rollouts to enhance pass@k. Our analysis identifies three key design principles: (1) difficulty-adaptive rollout can play an important role in expanding pass@k, beyond serving as an efficiency heuristic; (2) tree-based rollout outperforms parallel sampling in discovering correct answers; and (3) sentence-entropy-guided forking overcomes the localization phenomenon of token-level branching to maximize semantic diversity. Building on these insights, we propose DATPO (Difficulty-Adaptive Sentence-entropy-guided Tree-structured Policy Optimization). DATPO integrates difficulty-adaptive tree search with a sibling-diversity advantage term, explicitly promoting semantic diversity to expand reasoning coverage during training. Experiments on mathematical reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that DATPO outperforms baselines especially in pass@k, which directly translates to superior test-time scaling performance.
affiliations: Pohang University of Science and Technology (POSTECH)

ru.title: Древовидный поиск с адаптацией к сложности для расширения разнообразия рассуждений
ru.desc: DATPO — это метод обучения больших языковых моделей, который улучшает способность модели находить различные пути решения задач (pass@k). Подход использует адаптивный древовидный поиск, где сложность примеров влияет на глубину исследования, и направляет ветвление по энтропии предложений вместо токенов для большей семантической разнообразности. Метод добавляет специальный термин в функцию награды, явно стимулируя разнообразие решений во время обучения с подкреплением. Экспериментально показано, что DATPO превосходит базовые методы в расширении покрытия рассуждений и улучшает масштабируемость при тестировании.

en.title: Enhancing Reasoning Coverage with DATPO
en.desc: The paper presents DATPO, a method designed to enhance the reasoning capabilities of large models by improving their exploration during training. It introduces difficulty-adaptive tree-structured rollouts that utilize sentence-entropy to guide branching, which helps in discovering diverse and correct answers. The authors identify key principles that contribute to better reasoning coverage, such as the importance of adaptive rollouts and tree-based structures over traditional methods. Experiments show that DATPO significantly improves performance on mathematical reasoning tasks, particularly in terms of pass@k metrics, indicating better scalability during testing.

zh.title: DATPO：提升推理覆盖率的创新方法
zh.desc: DATPO是一种改进大型模型推理覆盖率的方法，采用难度自适应的树结构回滚和基于句子熵的分支优化。通过优化训练时的回滚结构设计，DATPO能够提高模型的推理覆盖率（pass@k），克服了传统方法在训练中探索有限的问题。研究表明，难度自适应回滚不仅提高效率，还能有效扩展推理能力；树结构回滚在发现正确答案方面优于并行采样；而基于句子熵的分叉方法则最大化了语义多样性。实验结果显示，DATPO在数学推理基准测试中表现优异，尤其是在pass@k方面，直接提升了测试时的扩展性能。

papers.title: DF26: We Cannot Tell Fake From Real Anymore
papers.abstract: Abstract A new benchmark for AI-generated public-speaking videos reveals that both humans and current detectors perform near chance, underscoring the need for robustness to modern generative distribution shifts.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small We introduce DF26, a novel benchmark for detecting AI-generated videos containing fully synthetic clips produced by recent text-to-video and image-to-video models. The videos capture single-person public-speaking scenarios, spanning direct-to-camera recordings, official statements, and studio interviews - 271 real and 2,420 synthetic videos generated by seven modern video models. The study on DF26 shows that human performance in detecting AI-generated videos, as well as state-of-the-art deepfake detectors, is close to random chance. Our results highlight the limitations of current evaluation protocols and motivate the need for benchmarks that explicitly measure robustness to modern generative model distribution shifts.
affiliations: Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Czech Technical University in Prague
Institute of Software Systems of the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine

ru.title: Когда детекторы видеосинтеза слепы: проблема надёжности перед вызовом генеративных моделей
ru.desc: Авторы представляют новый бенчмарк DF26 для выявления видео, созданных нейросетями, содержащий 271 реальное и 2420 синтетических видеороликов с выступлениями людей, сгенерированных семью современными моделями генерации видео. Исследование показало, что как люди, так и передовые детекторы дипфейков работают практически на уровне случайного угадывания при обнаружении AI-генерируемых видео. Результаты выявляют серьёзные ограничения существующих протоколов оценки и недостаток надёжности текущих методов детекции. Работа подчёркивает необходимость разработки более устойчивых к распределению генеративных моделей подходов обнаружения синтетического видеоконтента.

en.title: Rethinking Detection: The Challenge of AI-Generated Videos
en.desc: This paper introduces DF26, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the detection of AI-generated public-speaking videos. It includes a dataset of 271 real videos and 2,420 synthetic videos created by advanced text-to-video and image-to-video models. The findings reveal that both humans and existing deepfake detection systems struggle to distinguish between real and synthetic videos, performing at near random levels. This highlights the inadequacy of current evaluation methods and emphasizes the necessity for benchmarks that can effectively assess robustness against the evolving capabilities of generative models.

zh.title: 提升AI视频检测的鲁棒性
zh.desc: 本文介绍了DF26，这是一个新的基准，用于检测AI生成的公共演讲视频。研究发现，无论是人类还是现有的检测器在识别这些视频时的表现都接近随机水平，显示出当前检测技术的局限性。DF26包含271个真实视频和2420个由现代视频生成模型生成的合成视频，涵盖了多种演讲场景。研究结果强调了需要新的评估协议，以更好地衡量对现代生成模型分布变化的鲁棒性。
